ai.definition: RAG Pipelines are automated processes designed to aggregate and integrate information from various data sources to create or enhance knowledge bases used by artificial intelligence systems.
ai.howItWorks: These pipelines first identify relevant data sources, then extract and process the content, and finally store it in a structured format that can be queried by AI models. This involves tasks such as web scraping, natural language processing (NLP), and machine learning to ensure accurate and relevant data is included.
ai.problemSolved: The challenge of creating comprehensive and up-to-date knowledge bases for AI systems, which often require integration from multiple sources with varying formats and structures.
ai.manufacturing: The manufacturing process involves developing the pipeline software, integrating various NLP and machine learning tools, setting up data collection mechanisms, and establishing a robust storage system to handle large volumes of data.
ai.buildProcess: Building RAG Pipelines starts with defining the scope and requirements, followed by selecting appropriate data sources. Next, data extraction and preprocessing are performed using automated scripts or custom-built algorithms. Finally, the processed data is stored in databases optimized for querying by AI models.
ai.costDrivers: Costs associated with developing and maintaining RAG Pipelines include software development, hardware infrastructure (for storage and processing), licensing fees for NLP tools, and ongoing maintenance to ensure data accuracy and relevance.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is positive as the demand for comprehensive knowledge bases in AI applications continues to grow. However, challenges such as data privacy concerns and ensuring continuous data updates will need to be addressed.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks around data privacy (e.g., GDPR) and content accuracy may impact the design and implementation of RAG Pipelines. Compliance with these regulations is crucial for widespread adoption.
ai.risks: Risks include data quality issues, potential biases in data sources, and compliance risks related to data privacy laws. Additionally, maintaining up-to-date information can be challenging without robust monitoring systems.
ai.profitability: Profitability will depend on the specific application of RAG Pipelines and the value they provide to end-users or organizations. High demand for AI-driven knowledge bases could lead to significant revenue opportunities.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include advancements in NLP techniques, improvements in data processing speed, and enhanced integration with other AI technologies such as chatbots and recommendation systems.

subsystems.name: Ingestion and parsing
subsystems.role: turns raw documents into clean text with structure preserved.

subsystems.name: Chunking and embedding
subsystems.role: splits text into retrievable pieces and converts each into a numeric vector.

subsystems.name: Index stores
subsystems.role: hold the searchable representations of the corpus.
parts: optionally a graph or relational store of entities and relations

subsystems.name: Retriever
subsystems.role: finds the passages most relevant to a query.

subsystems.name: Generator
subsystems.role: writes the answer from the retrieved passages.

subsystems.name: Orchestration and evaluation
subsystems.role: runs the pipeline and measures whether it is actually good.

subsystems.name: Guardrails and access control
subsystems.role: keeps outputs grounded and stops users seeing documents they are not entitled to.

buildSteps.title: Collect the corpus
buildSteps.detail: Connect to the source systems — documents, tickets, databases — and pull the text plus permission metadata that must travel with every chunk.

buildSteps.title: Parse and clean
buildSteps.detail: Extract text from PDFs, web pages and scans; strip boilerplate; keep headings, tables and page numbers as structure.

buildSteps.title: Chunk
buildSteps.detail: Cut documents into passages of a few hundred words, with slight overlap so sentences aren't severed mid-thought.

buildSteps.title: Embed and index
buildSteps.detail: Run every chunk through an embedding model and write the vectors into an index tuned for fast approximate search; build a lexical index alongside it.

buildSteps.title: Build the retrieval path
buildSteps.detail: Encode the user's query, fetch candidates from both indexes, merge the rankings, and rerank the top few dozen with a slower, more accurate model.

buildSteps.title: Assemble the prompt
buildSteps.detail: Insert the winning passages with their source labels into a prompt that instructs the model to answer only from them and cite them.

buildSteps.title: Evaluate
buildSteps.detail: Score retrieval hits and answer faithfulness on a labelled question set, then tune chunk size, embedding model and reranker against those numbers.

buildSteps.title: Deploy with a freshness loop
buildSteps.detail: Re-embed changed documents on a schedule or on write, and invalidate stale vectors so answers track current data.
